historical_content: Concepts are foreshadowed as simplicial complexes; standard simplex/complex/chain language is introduced.
modern_assessment: Use only standard definitions after correcting terminology; chain cycles are not automatically concepts or symmetries.

historical_content: Calls X∧Y a higher-order concept and proposes measurement/distinguishing to separate X from Y.
modern_assessment: Useful semantic seed, but logical conjunction is not by itself simplicial gluing or statistical independence.

historical_content: Defines a concept as a connected simplicial complex whose vertices are pairwise connected by at least one edge; then claims such concepts are Hausdorff.
modern_assessment: The combinatorial definition is really a connected complete 1-skeleton condition; Hausdorffness requires a specified realization/topology and is not a property of a bare abstract complex.

historical_content: Concept order k is tied to k fixed attributes / p-adic balls.
modern_assessment: Attribute order is distinct from simplicial dimension; keep as a separate semantic grading.

topic: Matte-Blanco unfolding motivation and distinguishing operator
historical_content: Unfolding is motivated as successive entry of information into consciousness; the thesis defines a logical ∂ on an n-simplex by omitting one vertex and negating it.
modern_assessment: This ∂ is not the standard simplicial boundary. Treat it as a historical logical transformation requiring its own semantics.

historical_content: The thesis decomposes a logical triangle into lower-dimensional logical pieces and interprets ∂(green∧box) as allowing green and box to be distinguished.
modern_assessment: This is a logical decomposition; the geometric face picture and logical formula should be separated.

historical_content: After unfolding to lower-dimensional expressions, the thesis explicitly asks to build them back up by 'gluing' or 'integrating'.
modern_assessment: This is the central recoverability question; no category or universal property is specified historically.

historical_content: The thesis reconstructs X∧Y∧Z by conjunction of expressions associated with sides.
modern_assessment: This is Boolean reconstruction, not ordinary union of simplicial faces. It may be formalized as semantic gluing over a fixed face cover.

topic: tetrahedron from four triangular faces; integrator
classification: worked example + open question + unsupported claim
historical_content: States that a 3-simplex can be built by gluing its four 2-simplex faces and wonders about an 'integrator' like CW attachment.
modern_assessment: Under ordinary simplicial union the four faces give ∂Δ^3, not Δ^3. A filler/completion rule is required to add the 3-simplex.

topic: shared attributes and overlap of p-adic concepts
historical_content: Uses U∩V=W to represent shared attributes and pads unshared attributes by false/zero.
modern_assessment: Intersection/common support is a natural overlap object, but zero-padding is representation-dependent.

historical_content: Defines logical sets/topologies and a logical presheaf-like restriction system; states an aim to create larger complexes by gluing smaller concepts.
modern_assessment: Restriction data are naturally presheaf data. Genuine sheaf gluing additionally requires the sheaf existence-and-uniqueness axiom.

historical_content: Intersects concept topologies and proposes gluing compatible presheaf sections to create sheaves or higher-order concepts.
modern_assessment: Closest modern analogue is sheaf descent for compatible local sections; pairwise compatibility suffices only after the presheaf is known to be a sheaf.

topic: overlapping concepts C1 and C2; pink flower; rebuild after unfolding
historical_content: Unfolds overlapping concepts and says sections of a partition can be glued to regain X∧Y; uses pink∧flower as a higher-order concept.
modern_assessment: Recoverability needs retained cover/provenance and a specified logical gluing map; global object alone need not remember its decomposition.

historical_content: Logical triangles sharing an operator are 'glued' into exact squares; some pairs fail, and larger squares are formed by gluing smaller squares.
modern_assessment: This is an algebraic/diagrammatic gluing problem. A modern treatment should model the objects and compatibility morphisms explicitly; it is not automatically a simplicial pushout.
